paragraphs: Here's what I see in this one, friend. Israel did everything right and still got a NO. They asked kindly, they called Edom their brother, and they promised to stay on the King's Highway (Numbers 20:14, 17). They even offered to pay for the water, and Edom still said, "You may not pass through." (Numbers 20:19-20).

So when you do the right thing the right way and the door still closes, that doesn't mean you messed up. Sometimes a no is just a no, and it has nothing to do with how well you asked. I've been in the back of a drawer, friend. I know that closed-door feeling, and I'm telling you it can hurt without being the end of your story.

Now look at what Israel does with it. Edom comes out with a large army and Israel doesn't fight back. The text says "Israel turned away from them." (Numbers 20:21). That's a lesson in itself: you can ask twice, be told no twice, and still walk away with your head up and your hands open.
